I like Schedule I. The core gameplay loop is genuinely fun, and the first playthrough is a great experience. Building your operation, unlocking new products, and gradually expanding your business is extremely satisfying.

Unfortunately, the game’s post-launch development has been disappointing. Content updates take far too long to reach production, and when they finally arrive, they often feel shallow and disconnected from the rest of the game.

The mushroom update is a good example. It gives you another product to manufacture, but it does not meaningfully affect the game. It does not change how you operate, introduce interesting decisions, or interact with the existing systems in a meaningful way. You can ignore mushrooms entirely and lose virtually nothing from the experience.

The cartel update was a fantastic idea with poor execution. A rival criminal organization should create pressure, competition, danger, and meaningful rewards. Instead, the cartel mostly adds more chores and obstacles without giving the player much to gain. It feels less like a dynamic rival and more like an artificial way to slow progression and stretch out the existing content. There was so much potential here, which makes the final result especially disappointing.

I understand that this is largely the work of a solo developer, and that game development takes time. However, that explanation becomes less convincing after a game earns millions of dollars. Players bought the game in Early Access to support its continued development. At some point, it is reasonable to expect some of that success to be reinvested into additional development resources, faster production, and more substantial updates.

Early Access was originally presented as a way for players to fund promising games while developers continued building them. Increasingly, it feels like a way to earn most of a game’s revenue before delivering a finished product. Players are not simply buying what currently exists; they are buying into a promise that the game will continue growing. When development slows down and updates feel minimal, it creates the impression that the game has entered maintenance mode before it is anywhere close to finished.

I love Schedule I, and I want to see it reach its potential. That is exactly why its current development and management are so frustrating. The foundation is excellent, but the time, money, and momentum generated by the game’s success do not seem to be translating into the depth or pace of development that players were led to expect.

I’ve been playing Schedule One for a while now, and overall I genuinely enjoy it. The core gameplay loop is solid and it’s easy to sink hours into without noticing. If you like grind-heavy progression systems, this game will absolutely hook you. Watching your operation grow from nothing into something profitable is satisfying.

That said, the grind can feel excessive at times. A lot of the gameplay relies on repetitive manual tasks, and while that works early on, it starts to drag in the mid-to-late game. There needs to be deeper automation systems, something that lets you scale operations more efficiently once you’ve proven yourself.

Right now, it feels like you hit a ceiling. The game hints at building a serious empire, but you never quite reach that “kingpin” level. It would be great to expand progression so players can go full Tony Montana. Bigger networks, ability to export large quantities, larger territory control, higher risk/high reward systems, and more strategic management instead of constant micromanagement.

Schedule I has a really fun concept, and the first few hours are genuinely enjoyable. Building your empire from scratch, managing production, and expanding your operation feels satisfying at the beginning. The progression system keeps you interested, and it’s easy to see why the game has become so popular on Steam.

However, after spending more time with it, the gameplay starts to feel repetitive. A lot of the tasks become part of the same grind loop, and the excitement slowly wears off. While the management mechanics are solid, the game currently lacks enough variety to keep things fresh for long sessions.

Since it’s still in Early Access, some parts also feel unpolished, with rough mechanics and occasional bugs. It definitely has strong potential, but right now it feels more like a great idea that still needs more content and refinement.

Overall, it’s a good game with a unique concept, but it can become repetitive after a while.

Recommended, but with some reservations

Schedule 1 is a crime sim that mashes its dark subject matter and dirty jokes with surprisingly cozy management mechanics in a way that works really well, resulting in an extremely unique and highly amusing crafting game I happily sunk 100 hours into. Befriending my neighbors while getting them hooked on addictive substances grown in an apartment above a chinese restaurant is a goofy, satisfying hook, and leveling up my enterprise scratched an automation itch I don’t get to scratch often enough. This Early Access launch inevitably runs out of reasons to keep you playing since it’s quite clearly missing the back half of its campaign for now, and it has some bugs that give it a decidedly unpolished feel, but I still had a blast being an absolutely terrible human in the comfiest way possible.

(I'm reviewing this pre-Shrooms Update, post Halloween Update.)

I want to say I really like this game so far and I'm excited to see where it goes in the future. As it stands right now, it's not perfect but definitely promising. Some of the features could be improved before the final release of the game such as:

- Making the Cartel have more of a presence in Hyland Point
- Quality of life improvements to the Delivery and Dealers apps (which are confirmed to come in the future)
- Making employees faster and smarter (Chemists are expensive, yet lazy)
- More level up rewards for the late game (I'm sure this will come eventually though with new weapons, improved workstations, etc)
- Bug fixes (I'm sure 99% of the bugs will be fixed before release though)

Maybe the Cartel could have "events" around the map, like maybe if your dealers are being attacked, you have a couple hours to go and defend them or else your dealer will lose their product. And if you fend them off, you can lower their influence over the area. Stuff like this could help alleviate the problem of the Cartel dealers only showing up at 11:59 pm, and very occasionally ambushing you. The ambushes are very rare as of right now, which makes it harder to reduce the Cartel influence and unlock new areas. 
I actually got stuck in my first save file because I had unlocked all the customers in Westville and then betrayed the cartel, forcing me to wait every night at 11:59 for a Cartel dealer to pop out of their hideout so I can attack them.

Schedule I is a surprisingly deep and addictive simulation game that quickly pulls you into its unique gameplay loop. Starting from nothing and slowly building your own underground empire feels incredibly rewarding.

The progression system is one of the strongest parts of the game. Expanding your operation, upgrading equipment, and managing production creates a constant sense of growth. Every step forward feels earned and keeps you motivated to continue playing.

The open-world environment also adds a lot of immersion. Exploring the city, interacting with different characters, and carefully managing your business gives the game a dynamic sandbox feel.

Even in its current state, the game already offers a lot of fun and replayability. The developers clearly have strong ideas for expanding the mechanics and content, which makes the future of the game very promising.

If you enjoy sandbox management games with a bit of strategy and progression, Schedule I is definitely worth checking out.

You can make marijuana, cocaine, meth, and soon shrooms (in the newest update coming early to mid-December 2025). You can create so many different strains and combinations by mixing ingredients and name all the different strains yourself. This game just has everything you can possibly think of; I can't speak positively of it enough. Tyler recently released a cartel update, so now there is a cartel (Benzies) that warns you of selling drugs on "their" turf. You can either reject their proposal to work for them or accept. It makes the game feel more dangerous and fun, honestly. If you reject their proposal, they make your job of selling drugs a lot more dangerous for not only you but also your distributors.

Again, I love this game so much. I go through bouts where I get a little bored and then come back a couple of months later to new content and get addicted again. Is it worth the money? 100%, absolutely. You're also supporting a really awesome dev.

I really want to recommend this game, I spent quite a bit of time playing it and enjoyed some of it, yet I can't because it has glaring issues that aren't addressed. And with each passing update this game recieves I doubt they will if Tyler will continue making updates for the game based only on the community updates that add new mechanics that are barely fleshed out, instead of polishing already existing stuff and making it more enjoyable.

The game says that the whole drug dealing business in it is "dangerous" but the entire police department can be killed off on the first day if you put a tiny bit of effort, and the cartel barely does anything do hinder your operations. And even during the occurences during which the cartel actually DOES something besides leaving a graffiti or doing a deal (both of which I have seen like occur maybe 3 times through several of my playthroughs), like the gang jumping you or robbing the dealer, it usually happens so late into the game that it is barely an inconvenience.

Speaking of murdering the entire police station, the fact that you can steal the guns off of officers this early in the game completely destroys the balance of the game in two ways.

﻿﻿﻿1. You get late game weapons on practically the first day of the game which make any combat encounter trivial
﻿﻿﻿2. The weapons can be sold for a ridiculous (for the earlygame) price, which gives you way too much money than you should have in this stage of the game

There is no reason to diversify your products, as it is too much of a hassle for way too little of a return, and making one good product can practically catapult you to the endgame with the amount of money it can make.

And from one point of view it might seem weird of me complaining for having too much money, but the whole point of the game is to be making money, so getting so much early game makes the whole goal of the game nonexistant. Even if you consider destroying the cartel to be the main goal of the game, with the amount of money that you get from even just slightly optimising your operation makes it completely trivial and unrewarding (might be overexaggerating here, but I only got the satisfaction from the first time, because it was a tidious grind to get there).

The workers are just unfun to use. The only ones that are somewhat okay to work with are the botanists, and even then I wish that they weren't locked to only one locker for all of the resources that they need, because it makes organising how much each of the botanists need a chore, and handlers, but they have their own issues. The chemists feel like a downgraded version of the botanists but for chemistry work stations, in a sense that they can only have 3 work stations assigned to them, and they can't even bring the ingredients from the lockers to the work stations, making you have to manually put the ingredients into their work stations, and then manually take the output out. I would've understood if you could've assigned handlers to do the moving between stations, but you can't. Also the mixing abilities of chemists are abhorrent, so the fact that they can use the mixers is completely irrelevant, because if you want to make a mix that has more than 1 ingredient in it, you will have to do it manually as you can't just assign the chemist to do the proper mix because there is just no such option.

I understand that the workers are limiting so that we have to interact with the production of the drugs, but it fails at that, because at a certain point in the game all you do is order ingredients, repack the stations, deliver the product to dealers, repeat. Which makes for a very dull endgame that otherwise has a lot of potential.

And I know that the counterargument to bad workers is "just make the product by hand" but doing so is giving me carpal tunnel having to manually move 20 leaves into a cauldron to make cocaine, and if I miss a single leaf I have to restart the whole process. The early game suffers from the same issues a bit too, especially when you don't have a mk2 packager and mixer, but it makes sense as you have to work hard in the early game to make money. But the same doesn't apply when I am a rich cartel boss and can't for some reason just carry 20 leaves at once.

Also I wish that there was an actual time limit on doing the deals, because the night doesn't progress after 4 am, the deal timer is essentially endless (unless you forget you have deals and go to sleep), which removes all the pressure you did have on quickly finishing the deals.

I believe that the game can improve on every single one of the listed aspects, like making the police stronger, not letting you sell the guns you got from the cops cause I don't think a pawn shop should buy stolen items, making the cartel much more aggresive, having a supply/demand system where the products lose value the more of them you sell (also on a side note, please let us rename products, it is so infuriating when I misspell a product name and have to be stuck with it), make the workers consistent all around by letting for instance chemists pull ingredients from shelves and putting the finished product on shelves (like botanists do), make it so that the deal timer goes out before 4 am so that it is not endless.

I know that maybe some updates in the future will address some of the issues that the game has, like the police in the upcoming (hopefully) police rework update, but that should've been one of the first updates to come out.

I really like this game, but it's very depressing to see that the game's health isn't prioritized in the current updates that it recieves (that also take quite a long time to come out, but I don't judge here because I know that game development takes time), and instead the priority is on more side content instead of polishing the existing stuff.

[h1]An utter betrayal of promised dopamine.[/h1]

[b]The Good (Why it hooks you)[/b]
The first few hours are a masterpiece of tension. You’re huddled in a cramped, claustrophobic safehouse, meticulously weighing out single grams, micro-managing your cash, and genuinely sweating every time you see a cop. The gritty street-survival fantasy is running at 100%. It’s a phenomenal loop.

[b]The Bad (The Betrayal)[/b]
Then, you unlock more properties.
The exact millisecond you buy properties and get a high-tier distributor automated, the game completely runs out of gas. The survival mechanics evaporate, and the entire experience pivots into a mindless, idle clicker. You aren’t a kingpin; you’re just a bored data analyst sitting in an empty warehouse watching numbers go up and waiting on money-laundering timers to tick down.

The difficulty curve flatlines so hard it feels like a scam. I got so bored with the lack of stakes that I literally killed my entire customer base with toxic experimental batches and logged off for good.

I love the game, I really do. It's already become a go-to comfort pick for me and my boyfriend to just banter on with good vibes. Despite giving it my thumbs up, I still think there could be some genuine improvements to the game.

I am sorely disappointed in the presence of the Cartel, or lack thereof, once unlocking them within the story. They barely show up and to decrease the influence of the Cartel in certain districts, we had to camp certain doors at midnight to kill a Cartel dealer that only briefly would leave the building and go back inside, unless you managed to knock them out in time. It wasn't long after until we realised that having the influence completely down to 0 had little to none impact on the story. 

Of course I know the game is still in early access and being fixed, though, the longer we played the same game file, the more things got buggy. We had to abandon one of our save files because eventually cars were literally flying, turning upside down, doors that shouldn't be open were open, etc. 

We usually played through the bugs and didn't mind them all that much, though some of them were quite frustrating and so unavoidably frequent, it almost got us to ragequit a couple of times;

Sometimes my friend would get arrested by police and captured even if he wasn't anywhere near them, needlessly losing bagged products and money in the process.

The game would often crash for the person who wasn't hosting the game and upon getting back into the game, items and money would have disappeared from their inventory.

We grinded so hard for the manor, I was so hyped to see it and did everything in my power to explore it myself before looking at it online or anywhere else. But my disappointment to see the manor so empty and bland, with nothing inside like a kitchen or a bathroom or anything that could've been built in (like the bungalow's kitchen) was so disappointing and such a let-down, it was so anti-climactic that I closed the game without saving it and haven't been back online yet.

I do feel like the manor shouldn't be unlockable after the end of the game, once you've fully gotten rid of the Cartel. I felt like there was no point to the manor because the game was already done.

Regardless of all my criticism to the game, I still enjoyed my time thoroughly on it and it's got a cosy vibe to it that I will definitely revisit again at some point. Keep up the good work!

Fun game but the community is seemingly made up of zoomers that don't care about the progress of the game and just want mor drugz. Police are essentially the center of the game loop and they are really terrible, you can escape them really easily and there is little to no ramp up in response. You escape the same way every time. Months ago a community vote chose shrooms instead if I recall correctly which is totally unnecessary as there are already several drugs and mixes in the game. Then we got cartels which is super awesome because the system is fair enough as it is except that when you are attacked in front of the police you will be shot for retaliating. You also generally escape or kill them the same way every time which isnt't particularly satisfying. The goal is to essentially remove them from the game by removing their influence which at least adds another loop to the game, but it just feels like a progression toilet. Now we have yet another community vote where better police are on the table, aaaaaaand everyone voted for 'special customers' which is another unneeded loop in the game. We need better police AI, targeted raids, intel on said raids where you have limited time to move your goods/operation or bribe, and a more dynamic system in general for police behavior. 

Presently, while the game is a lot of fun for a while I had banked my goodwill toward the game and returned to it on the premise that eventually they would flesh out the base systems in the game but instead we keep getting semi fleshed-out content expansions which, while cool, takes the game in the opposite direction of feeling complete in my opinion. 

You'll probably have fun with it though co-op is pretty limited, you will likely enjoy the novelty aspect of the game for a good 10-20 hours depending on your personality.

The game feels really nice to play. It's pretty in depth for what it is and needs some planning how to progress and sell your drugs.

Building up your empire feels rewarding too, you start small and become powerful step by step. Progression is somewhat time-gated but it's not too annoying or harsh.

I like the updates that are coming out albeit they feel a bit slow and rushed at times. The game became quite buggy in multiplayer which makes only the host eligible to pay off debt, pay the cartel, buy property, etc. That really sucks but can usually be fixed with restarting the session or waiting for a bug fix update.

For the price it's great value and I really wish for the game to get harder and more risky. Police feels braindead at times - they are no threat. Maybe a helicopter or SWAT units could mix things up? The cartel is a great idea, just not that fleshed out sadly.

All in all, despite my criticism, it's still a recommendation!

It might be great in the future, but so far it’s really too small. The first few hours are amazing, but after about 10 hours you start to exhaust everything the game has to offer, and progress slows down a lot. You don’t feel like Heisenberg at the end more like a small local-town drug dealer and I doubt that will change with the full release.

Dealing yourself is much more profitable than using dealers. The cartel update seems fun, but the lockout of other zones until you arbitrarily lower their influence for clients to buy from you is dumb especially since the only reliable way to do it is by exploiting bugs. Buying spray is limited to one a day or something like that, which makes it very boring and slow.

Would be closer to neutral review but no such option exists on Steam. Honeymoon phase is neat and exists for every game but unfortunately tedium gets worse and worse over time.

It feels like a DarkRP drug role that received its own game - with decently fun minigames. But they quickly overstay their welcome, especially when scaling up operations it isn't simply fun to do this ♥♥♥♥ tens of times over and over, and some parts of the drug manufacturing that are annoying cannot be skipped over.

The balancing with cash/credit is terrible - I unlocked cocaine before I even managed to afford the barn. Mushrooms have weird place where they are located after meth and shortly before coke is available, require more hands-on than even weed while barely more profitable. Robbing guns from cops feels like an exploit given how much money it can give so early on. For most time, I was artificially blocked from buying new ♥♥♥♥ and having to carry tens of thousands of dollars while money laundering drip-fed me credit balance that was being taken by some produce that you HAVE to buy for credit balance until much later on.

Cartel was non-existent for me through my gameplay. I seen TB roll up to me, told him to ♥♥♥♥ off becoming enemies with Benzies, never seen him ever again nor my dealers were attacked even once. Combat is a meme in this game in general, even before guns you can easily whack entire police force with a baseball bat.

Mixing anything 'fun' and expensive takes far too much time if playing 'by the rules' turning a single 20-piece batch can take total in-game day. The experience could be less miserable by having either a feeder-hopper with ability to queue up to 8 ingredient 'batches' or bundled together for tier 3 of the mixer.

Automation feels clunky and handicapped - the amount of objects that the workers handle is miserable. I seen guides explaining how to automate the mixing and there is no way to just set a recipe and let workers handle the recipe until the final product is reached, it requires some stupid daisychaining that I would expect to be done from a mod, not an official paid game.

It's understandable that this is EA and 'this is done by a single guy and they just got the studio' yaddayadda I get it, but does not help that this concept generally does not feel fun beyond few hours in. I've tried multiple runs to 'finish' the game but i got tired of it each time because it turns into a boring slog at midpoint. I think fixing balance of drugs and income first, maybe making police less of a pushover, would actually be more healthy in long run than adding new content that essentially sits on islands.

Beyond design issues, there are a lot of technical issues as well - police respawning after reloading a save, laundering operations disappearing or being rollbacked, vendors dialogue prompts disappearing and trash items getting stuck on objects that cannot be picked up until the object is redeployed. Those are the things that I've experienced myself in the latest run. If the Cartel is supposed to appear more often and not that I accidentally curbstomped them so hard they just hid 24/7, I guess that is a bug too.

The performance for the game with graphics that is on the level with Unturned is atrocious. I have no idea why this game runs like ♥♥♥♥ until everything is set to lowest and even then it stutters during combat.

Hoping the developers make priority of making game feel like a proper game and not just a tech demo - I appreciate them taking the 'community votes' as a way to be close with players and let them decide what comes up next, however the devs still need to have a solid grasp what actually game needs the most given technical and design issues will just permeate to every next content update.

I absolutely trust the dev, and think this game is very good... but what kills me is the performance. My game is either bugged or the optimization in this game is horrendous as of now. With the PC i got, there's no excuse for getting below 60 fps on minimum graphic settings.
Gotta let this one cook for a little longer.

I wanted to come back and re-review Schedule 1 since I recompleted the 100%. For context, I bought this game right when it dropped in Spring 2025 and have loved all, if not most of it. I did take a long break from playing and the last time I played was prior to shrooms and weather being added (among other additions). 

I still fully agree with my first review of this game, SUMMARY: when it first dropped you had to be there and it was certainly a contender for 2025 GOY in my humble opinion. The hype and community around the time of release was insane and it was so fun to be a part of. 

That said, I think the only issue I have with the game is the same as I did back then; the mid-to-late gameplay is slow and a bit boring at times (for me). You can definitely progress the game far enough and still have fun (it is a sandbox game afterall!) but for me it just lacks something. I’m not sure if the map isn’t interactive or even immersive enough or if it’s something else that isn’t yet fully fleshed out. But once you get to a certain point financially and with automated farms/properties, it just fizzles out for me. I thought going into my most recent playthrough that the addition of the Cartel would make things interesting, but it honestly didn’t. At first I was taken back by their presence, but I was then quickly able to overpower them and they truly posed no challenge to me or my dealers. 

I know that the game is made by one developer/a smaller team, so there’s absolutely no hate for them because I’m happy with all they’ve done thus far. I’m looking forward to future content updates since I know the community is active and TVGS truly listens to and involves the community in the update progress. So trust me, I’ll inevitably be back to re-complete the 100% if and when new stuff gets added. 

Since I know several people on my friends list have played the game, I wanted to share a few ideas I had for future updates and would love to hear anyone's thoughts or any ideas you’ve had. So far I’ve thought about:

- Being able to go into more buildings, especially residential (not having to call someone down from inside like the Apartment Building)
- Bikes or scooters for cheaper transportation
- Backpacks for more storage on your person
- Can eat items like donuts or addy (and they give special effects like mixed products do)
- Can throw or drop items from your inventory 
- Can sell items to more than just Mick (why can’t I sell clothes to the lady at Thrifty Threads?!)
